description: Source code for machines: a Python framework binding parts, dimensions, motion, controls and tests into a whole.
rules: Machinome 0.8.1 (released 2026-10-10) corrects 0.8.0 (2026-10-05), which continues 0.7.1 (2026-09-27); 0.7.0 (2026-09-23) was the first Machinome release, continuing solid-node 0.6.0. 0.8 is a lean core: CAD kernels and node families are extras, every name is imported from its module, the comparison engines are brep and mesh, and the document format is unchanged; it is licensed GPL-2.0-or-later or CERN-OHL-S-2.0-or-later at the recipient's choice. docs/project/upgrading.rst lists every breaking change from 0.7. Use the machinome distribution, machinome Python imports and command, [tool.machinome] configuration and MACHINOME_* replacements for former SOLID_NODE_* settings. No old command or import aliases are installed. See docs/project/upgrading.rst for retained SOLID_BUILD_DIR and SOLID_TEST_* settings.

A project declares its default model or named models in [tool.machinome] in pyproject.toml. Node commands accept a model name, package.module:Class, or file reference. Each named model has its own build directory; machinome models lists them.

Declare typed build parameters in machinome.parameters and child nodes in the class body. render() builds and places the structure at rest; simulate() expresses runtime pose. Constructor-based nodes remain supported.
Import ports and Time from machinome.motion.ports, joints from machinome.motion.joints, and Driver, State, Instruction and Sim from machinome.simulation.

Class-body joints use their body's own frame. Placement-site joints use the declaring parent's frame. Relations bind coordinates through declared laws; geometry, tests and publication share those relationships.

Choose simulation by the machine: plain Sim(model, dt=...) steps inputs, Time.running() selects running mechanics, and a State anywhere in the tree selects clocked Sim(model) without dt. Time.elapsed() adds non-wrapping seconds; under a clocked root it supplies the banked clock.

Import every name from its module: the root of machinome.node exports nothing, so write from machinome.node.assembly import AssemblyNode, from machinome.node.cadquery import CadQueryNode, from machinome.node.frames import Frame; each node type is one module under machinome.node (cadquery, build123d, step, molejo, solid2, openscad, jscad, stl, freecad). Each CAD kernel and node family is an extra named for that module: pip install "machinome[cadquery]", [build123d], [step], [molejo], [brep], [mesh], [openscad], [solid2], [jscad], [stl], [freecad] or [all]; a bare install carries no kernel and a missing one is refused naming its extra. FreeCAD itself is found through MACHINOME_FREECAD_ROOT.

Two comparison engines: brep (machinome.engine.brep, B-rep parts from CadQuery, build123d, STEP, sheet leaves and molejo, over the OCCT kernel) and mesh (machinome.engine.mesh, triangle meshes, manifold3d). machinome test --brep (default) or --mesh, else SOLID_TEST_ENGINE=brep|mesh; SOLID_TEST_KERNEL is refused. B-rep-only fusions stay B-rep; others use the mesh engine. shape() returns the OCCT TopoDS_Shape; wrap it with cadquery.Shape.cast(...) before calling CadQuery methods. intersect_shapes, fuse_shapes, placed_shape, solid_count and solid_volume are imported from machinome.engine.brep. Leaf bases LeafNode, BrepLeafNode (machinome.node.brep_leaf), SheetLeafNode and FlexibleNode are a declared contract, version 3.

OpenSCAD (the executable) and the openscad extra are needed only for the OpenSCAD family, Solid2Node (machinome.node.solid2, extra solid2) and OpenScadNode (machinome.node.openscad), and, with the OpenSCAD viewer (machinome.viewer.openscad, the distribution machinome-viewer-openscad, which the openscad and solid2 extras install, or the viewer-openscad extra alone), for the default viewer of machinome snapshot; machinome snapshot --viewer web needs neither, and --renderer is refused naming --viewer. A project may name its viewer with viewer = "web" under [tool.machinome]. A build writes a .scad only for an OpenSCAD-family part.
Build freshness tracks each node's contributing source, including project-local imports. Several node classes may share a file without automatically invalidating unrelated sibling geometry.

Place whole-assembly integrity assertions at the root when that is the contract: assertNoSolidInterference and assertNoDisconnectedSolids already descend their subtrees. assertNoPairwiseIntersections is deprecated.

The browser viewer is machinome.viewer.web, the repository's distribution machinome-viewer, installed by pip install "machinome[viewer]" and numbered with the framework; it is not published on npm. machinome develop requires it; --no-web builds and watches without it. Check machinome viewer for the installed API and supported documentVersions. Embed an exported page in an iframe, or load machinome-viewer.js and call MachinomeViewer.mount(target, documentUrl, options); mountInspector() adds a collapsible assembly sidebar. The framework reaches it through its seam of viewers, machinome.viewer, in its own process, and no entry point names it. Its command is machinome viewer describe|serve|capture; machinome viewer alone prints the report.

The matching viewer is 0.8.1, API 29, reading document schemas 1-13; running documents are 5-7 or 9-13 (new running exports declare 11, source-timed motion, 12 when they carry a Follow relation, or 13 when a running Bound uses finite profile contact) and clocked documents are 8. Check the installed package with machinome viewer.

Frames and mates: a part declares a connector in its own rest frame with Frame(at=, z=, x=) from machinome.node.frames; an assembly places a directly declared child with child.frame.on(fixed_frame, Revolute(...)) or Prismatic(...), with no freedom to hold a bought part, or with child.joint to attach an existing scalar joint. A mate compiles at realization to the rest placement, a joint on the child and a coordinate on the assembly under the mate's name; a freedom's axis and range may be one function of the assembly. Read them back with resolved_frames(node) and declared_mates(cls). The published document is unchanged.

machinome vet [reference] [--tests] [--json] checks statically that a project stays inside the machinome universe (the framework, its kernels and a pure stdlib tier): no process, socket, dynamic import or file write, and every declared STL, STEP, OpenSCAD or JSCAD source under the project root. It reads only the project's bytes and machinome/vet/universe.toml and reports one verdict per model, pure or findings by path and line.

Running-only clearance laws: Play(low, high) retains a follower through backlash from one source; Follow(lower=, upper=) retains a coordinate between two independently moving authored surfaces and needs matching lower and upper Bound relations on that coordinate. Unsupported source ancestry is refused, not approximated.

Finite profile contact: import ConvexProfile and profile_overlap from machinome.simulation.profile. profile_overlap(left, right, left_angle, right_angle, left_xy=, right_xy=) returns 1.0 on inclusive contact of two authored convex planar profiles, else 0.0. Symbolically it is admitted only as a term in a running Bound's limit expression and refused elsewhere. It is pointwise, not continuous collision detection, and does not prove the profiles cover installed parts.

The mechanics helpers are machinome.mechanics, installed by pip install "machinome[mechanics]" (the distribution machinome-mechanics, numbered with the framework): gear, screw, crank, cam, indexing, delta, linkage, rolling and belt formulas. Angles are degrees. Each helper accepts numbers and the framework's symbolic values, so one formula serves a numeric pose and a relation law, for example crank.turn.drives(piston.rise, law=piston_law) where the law calls piston_height. The package supplies formulas only; the project supplies dimensions, reference frames, signs, branch selection and assembly facts; the framework never imports the helpers.

The machinome skills for assistants that read Agent Skills, machinome and machinome-simulate, are installed by pip install "machinome[skills]" then machinome skills install [path] [--tools all|none|ids] [--personal] [--force], which copies each skill into the directories the named tools read (ids as OpenSpec's, and agents for .agents/skills/); machinome skills update rewrites older copies and machinome skills list prints the tools. A copy carries metadata installed-by: machinome-skills; a skill without it is refused unless --force, and nothing is deleted.

A film of a machine is made with pip install "machinome[movie]", then machinome movie setup (Node 22 or newer, the user's; FFmpeg and Playwright's Chromium are separate steps). Declare a movie in Python with machinome.movie (Movie, Chapter, Shot, Narration, Take and the stage's Set, Slot and Element) and list it in the project's pyproject.toml; machinome movie check|speech|preview|render|build|live takes an episode.yaml, a movie.json or a project directory and a movie name; the browser viewer installed beside it draws every frame.

Machinome Studio is machinome.studio, the repository's distribution machinome-studio, installed by pip install "machinome[studio]" and numbered with the framework; machinome studio --projects-dir PATH opens its project hub on 127.0.0.1, the port from --port, FLOOR_PORT or ~/.config/machinome-studio/config.toml, else 9000. It needs the OpenSpec CLI on the PATH and a logged-in Claude Code, OpenCode or Codex; a project selects its profile and agents' runtimes in [tool.machinome-studio] of its pyproject.toml.
Keep geometry and operating claims tied to runnable examples and tests. Simulated motion is not a claim of physical manufacturing validation.

The manual is organised by reader intent: start pages, a ten-chapter tutorial building a tally counter under docs/tutorial/, how-to guides under docs/howto/, concept pages under docs/concepts/, examples, reference and project pages.
